Manage your PKIaaS certificate authorities and keys. AI agents: start with the [agent guide](agents.md), or run `pkiaas help agents`.

## Global flags

| Flag | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | bool | print the result, or the error, as JSON |
| `-h`, `--help` | bool | show help for the command; with `--json`, as JSON |

## Environment

| Variable | Use |
|---|---|
| `PKIAAS_TOKEN` | a token to use instead of the stored login (e.g. in CI); never print it |
| `PKIAAS_SERVER` | the server to use when `--server` isn't given, e.g. https://pkiaas.io |
| `PKIAAS_CA` | the ID of the CA that commands work in when `--ca` isn't given, instead of the active CA |

Exit codes and error codes are listed in the [agent guide](agents.md#exit-codes).

## pkiaas ca

List your certificate authorities, show one, get its certificate, set the active one.

```
pkiaas ca [flags]
```

Commands:

- [`pkiaas ca cert`](reference.md#pkiaas-ca-cert)
- [`pkiaas ca list`](reference.md#pkiaas-ca-list)
- [`pkiaas ca set`](reference.md#pkiaas-ca-set)
- [`pkiaas ca show`](reference.md#pkiaas-ca-show)

## pkiaas ca cert

Save a CA's certificate, or its chain, to a PEM file.

```
pkiaas ca cert --out FILE [--chain] [--ca ID] [flags]
```

Save the certificate of a CA, by default the active CA, to a PEM file. With `--chain`, the file holds the CA's
certificate followed by the certificates that issued it, up to the root; for a root CA that is its certificate
alone.

The chain is what a server needs beside a certificate the CA issued (e.g. nginx's ssl_certificate after the
certificate, or Apache's SSLCertificateChainFile), and what `pkiaas pkcs12 create --chain` adds to a PKCS#12
file. The CA certificate alone, of a root CA, is what clients add to their trust store.

Certificates are public: the file is readable by everyone, like any certificate. An existing file is only
replaced with `--force`. A CA waiting for its signed certificate fails with ca_not_signed.

This command calls the PKIaaS server and needs a login.

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ca` | string | the CA to work in, by its ID from `pkiaas ca list` (default: `PKIAAS_CA`, else the active CA) |
| `--chain` | bool | write the CA's certificate followed by the certificates that issued it |
| `--force` | bool | replace the file if it exists |
| `-o`, `--out` | string | the PEM file to write. Required. |
| `--server` | string | the PKIaaS server (default: the last one you logged in to) |

Examples:

```sh
pkiaas ca cert --out ca.pem
pkiaas ca cert --chain --out chain.pem --json
pkiaas ca cert --ca a1B2c3D4e5 --chain --out chain.pem --json
```

With `--json`, the result is an object with these fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | the CA's ID |
| `name` | string or null | the CA's name |
| `file` | string | the PEM file written |
| `chain` | boolean | whether the file holds the chain (`--chain`): the CA's certificate followed by those that issued it |
| `certificates` | integer | how many certificates the file holds |

Side effects:

- writes the `--out` file (certificates are public, so it is readable by everyone)

## pkiaas ca list

List the CAs you have access to.

```
pkiaas ca list [flags]
```

List the certificate authorities your account has access to: your own, and those you were invited to, by
name. The ID is what commands take to name a CA. The active CA, which commands work in unless told otherwise, is
marked with *.

This command calls the PKIaaS server and needs a login.

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--server` | string | the PKIaaS server (default: the last one you logged in to) |

Examples:

```sh
pkiaas ca list
pkiaas ca list --json
```

With `--json`, the result is an array of objects with these fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | the CA's ID, which commands take to name the CA |
| `name` | string or null | the CA's name (its certificate's common name) |
| `signed` | boolean | false while the CA waits for its signed certificate to be imported |
| `validTo` | string or null | when the CA's certificate expires (ISO 8601, UTC); null if unsigned |
| `active` | boolean | whether it is the active CA, which commands work in unless told otherwise |

## pkiaas ca set

Set the active CA.

```
pkiaas ca set ID [flags]
```

Set the active CA, which commands work in unless told otherwise, by its ID from `pkiaas ca list`. It is kept
on this computer, for this server, until `pkiaas logout`; it doesn't change the CA you work in on the website.

This command calls the PKIaaS server and needs a login.

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--server` | string | the PKIaaS server (default: the last one you logged in to) |

Examples:

```sh
pkiaas ca set a1B2c3D4e5
pkiaas ca set a1B2c3D4e5 --json
```

With `--json`, the result is an object with these fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `server` | string | the server |
| `id` | string or null | the active CA's ID; null if the account has no CAs |
| `name` | string or null | the active CA's name |
| `source` | string | why it is active: set (with `pkiaas ca set`, or at login), website (the CA last used on the website), first (the first CA by name), or none |

Side effects:

- keeps the CA as the active one in the CLI's config.json, for this server

## pkiaas ca show

Show a CA's details, by default the active CA's.

```
pkiaas ca show [--ca ID] [flags]
```

Show a CA's details: its key, certificate (serial, thumbprint, validity), how many certificates it has issued
that are still valid, and the URLs of its public services (certificate, chain, CRL, OCSP, time stamping, CPS page
and Windows enrollment).

Without `--ca` or `PKIAAS_CA`, it shows the active CA: the CA that commands work in unless told otherwise. It is the
one set with `pkiaas ca set` (or at login), on this computer for this server. Until one is set, it is the CA you
last worked in on the website. The result's source says how the CA was chosen. When the account has no CAs, the
id, the name and the details are null, and source is none.

This command calls the PKIaaS server and needs a login.

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ca` | string | the CA to work in, by its ID from `pkiaas ca list` (default: `PKIAAS_CA`, else the active CA) |
| `--server` | string | the PKIaaS server (default: the last one you logged in to) |

Examples:

```sh
pkiaas ca show
pkiaas ca show --json
pkiaas ca show --ca a1B2c3D4e5 --json
```

With `--json`, the result is an object with these fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `server` | string | the server |
| `id` | string or null | the CA's ID; null if the account has no CAs |
| `name` | string or null | the CA's name (its certificate's common name) |
| `source` | string | how the CA was chosen: flag (`--ca`), environment (`PKIAAS_CA`), or as the active CA: set (with `pkiaas ca set`, or at login), website (the CA last used on the website), first (the first CA by name); none if the account has no CAs |
| `signed` | boolean or null | false while the CA waits for its signed certificate to be imported |
| `hsm` | boolean or null | whether the CA's private key is on the user's HSM rather than on the platform |
| `keyType` | string or null | the algorithm of the CA's key, as OpenSSL names it, e.g. rsaEncryption, id-ecPublicKey, ML-DSA-65 |
| `keySize` | integer or null | the key size in bits (the curve size for EC keys); null where it doesn't apply, e.g. ML-DSA |
| `signatureAlgorithm` | string or null | the algorithm of the CA certificate's signature, as OpenSSL names it |
| `serial` | string or null | the CA certificate's serial number (hex); null if unsigned |
| `thumbprint` | string or null | the CA certificate's SHA-1 fingerprint (hex), as Windows shows it; null if unsigned |
| `validFrom` | string or null | when the CA's certificate became valid (ISO 8601, UTC); null if unsigned |
| `validTo` | string or null | when the CA's certificate expires (ISO 8601, UTC); null if unsigned |
| `activeCertificates` | integer or null | how many certificates the CA issued that have neither expired nor been revoked |
| `policyOid` | string or null | the certificate policy OID the CA puts in the certificates it issues; null if none |
| `cep` | boolean or null | whether Windows certificate enrollment (CEP/CES) is on |
| `urls` | object or null | the CA's public services; null until the CA is signed |
| `urls.certificate` | string | the CA's certificate (DER), as the certificates it issues name it (AIA caIssuers) |
| `urls.chain` | string | the CA's certificate and those that issued it (PKCS#7, DER) |
| `urls.crl` | string | the CRL (CRL distribution point) |
| `urls.ocsp` | string | the OCSP responder (AIA OCSP) |
| `urls.timestamp` | string | the RFC 3161 time-stamping service |
| `urls.cps` | string | the CA's public page: its certification practice statement and downloads |
| `urls.cep` | string or null | Windows certificate enrollment (CEP/CES) with a user name and password; null when it is off |
| `urls.cepCertificate` | string or null | Windows certificate enrollment (CEP/CES) with a client certificate; null when it is off |

## pkiaas csr

Create certificate signing requests on this computer.

```
pkiaas csr [flags]
```

Commands:

- [`pkiaas csr create`](reference.md#pkiaas-csr-create)

## pkiaas csr create

Create a certificate signing request (CSR).

```
pkiaas csr create --key FILE (--cn NAME | --subject DN) [flags]
```

Create a PKCS#10 certificate signing request signed with your private key.

The subject is either just a common name (`--cn`) or a full distinguished name (`--subject`), in RFC 4514 form
("CN=host.example.com,O=Example,C=US") or OpenSSL's form ("/C=US/O=Example/CN=host.example.com"). In Git Bash,
use the RFC 4514 form: Git Bash rewrites arguments that start with "/".

Subject alternative names (`--san`, repeatable) are dns:NAME, ip:ADDRESS, email:ADDRESS or uri:URI; without a
prefix the kind is guessed. If no `--san` is given and the common name is a DNS name, it is added as one,
because browsers and most clients only check SANs. With `--san`, list the common name too.

Without `--out` the CSR is printed (inside the JSON result with `--json`).

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--cn` | string | the subject's common name. Not with `--subject`. |
| `--force` | bool | replace the file if it exists |
| `-k`, `--key` | string | the private key file. Required. |
| `--key-passphrase-env` | string | read the key passphrase from this environment variable. Not with `--key-passphrase-file`. |
| `--key-passphrase-file` | string | read the key passphrase from this file's first line (- for standard input). Not with `--key-passphrase-env`. |
| `-o`, `--out` | string | the file to save the CSR in (default: print it) |
| `--san` | string, repeatable | a subject alternative name (repeatable) |
| `--subject` | string | the subject's distinguished name. Not with `--cn`. |

Examples:

```sh
pkiaas csr create --key server.key --cn www.example.com --san www.example.com --san example.com --out server.csr
pkiaas csr create --key server.key --key-passphrase-env KEY_PASSPHRASE --subject "CN=www.example.com,O=Example,C=US" --san ip:192.0.2.10 --json
```

With `--json`, the result is an object with these fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | string, optional | the CSR file; left out without `--out` |
| `keyType` | string | the key's type, as in `pkiaas key types` |
| `subject` | string | the subject's distinguished name, RFC 4514 form |
| `sans` | string[] | the subject alternative names, each as kind:value (dns:, ip:, email:, uri:) |
| `publicKeySha256` | string | the SHA-256 of the public key (DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo), in hex |
| `csr` | string, optional | the CSR in PEM form; only without `--out` |

Side effects:

- writes the `--out` file, if given

## pkiaas help

Show help for a command, or the guide for AI agents.

```
pkiaas help [command... | agents] [flags]
```

Show help for a command. `pkiaas help agents` shows the guide for AI agents: how to run pkiaas without
prompts, keep secrets out of transcripts, log in, and handle each error code.

With `--json`, the command and those under it are described as JSON: every flag, example, result field, side
effect, exit code and error code. `pkiaas <command> --help --json` does the same.

Examples:

```sh
pkiaas help agents
pkiaas help --json
pkiaas help --json key create
```

## pkiaas key

Create private keys on this computer.

```
pkiaas key [flags]
```

Commands:

- [`pkiaas key create`](reference.md#pkiaas-key-create)
- [`pkiaas key types`](reference.md#pkiaas-key-types)

## pkiaas key create

Create a private key.

```
pkiaas key create --out FILE [flags]
```

Create a private key and save it as a PKCS#8 PEM file that only you can read.

The key is encrypted with a passphrase (AES-256-CBC, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with 600,000 iterations) unless
`--no-passphrase` is given. Run `pkiaas key types` to list the key types.

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--force` | bool | replace the file if it exists |
| `--no-passphrase` | bool | save the key unencrypted |
| `-o`, `--out` | string | the file to save the key in. Required. |
| `--passphrase-env` | string | read the key passphrase from this environment variable. Not with `--passphrase-file`. |
| `--passphrase-file` | string | read the key passphrase from this file's first line (- for standard input). Not with `--passphrase-env`. |
| `--type` | string | the key type. Default: `rsa-2048`. |

Examples:

```sh
pkiaas key create --out server.key
pkiaas key create --type ml-dsa-65 --out pq.key --passphrase-env KEY_PASSPHRASE --json
pkiaas key create --type ec-p256 --out ci.key --no-passphrase --json
```

With `--json`, the result is an object with these fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | the key file |
| `type` | string | the key type, as in `pkiaas key types` |
| `encrypted` | boolean | whether the key is encrypted with a passphrase |
| `publicKeySha256` | string | the SHA-256 of the public key (DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo), in hex; the CSR and PKCS#12 commands report the same value |

Side effects:

- writes the `--out` file, readable by the owner only

## pkiaas key types

List the key types.

```
pkiaas key types [flags]
```

List the key types `pkiaas key create --type` accepts: RSA, EC, Ed25519 and Ed448, and the post-quantum
ML-DSA and SLH-DSA types. PKIaaS signs CSRs for all of them, but few clients accept the post-quantum types yet.

Examples:

```sh
pkiaas key types --json
```

With `--json`, the result is an array of objects with these fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | the name to give to `--type` |
| `description` | string | what the key type is |
| `default` | boolean | whether it is the default type |

## pkiaas login

Log in to a PKIaaS server.

```
pkiaas login [flags]
```

Log in to a PKIaaS server, by default https://pkiaas.io or the server of your last login.

Your browser opens to log in and to allow the CLI. On a computer without a browser (e.g. over SSH), use `--device`:
it shows a code to enter on another device. The token is kept in the system keyring, or where there is none in a
file only you can read. `PKIAAS_TOKEN`, if set, is used instead of a stored token.

Login shows the active CA, which commands work in unless told otherwise: the one set before with `pkiaas ca set`,
else the CA you last worked in on the website. Change it with `pkiaas ca set`.

A person has to approve the login in their browser. AI agents: ask the user to run it, see `pkiaas help agents`.

This command calls the PKIaaS server and needs the user to take part.

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--device` | bool | log in by entering a code in a browser on another device |
| `--server` | string | the PKIaaS server, e.g. https://pkiaas.io (default: the last one you logged in to) |

Examples:

```sh
pkiaas login
pkiaas login --device
pkiaas login --server https://pki.example.com
```

With `--json`, the result is an object with these fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `server` | string | the server logged in to |
| `email` | string or null | the account's email address |
| `displayName` | string or null | the account's name |
| `provider` | string | the identity provider the account signs in with, e.g. google |
| `storedIn` | string | where the token is kept: the system keyring, or the path of the owner-only file |
| `activeCaId` | string or null | the active CA's ID, which commands work in unless told otherwise; null if the account has no CAs |
| `activeCaName` | string or null | the active CA's name |

Side effects:

- stores the token in the system keyring or an owner-only file
- remembers the server for later commands
- keeps the active CA: the one set before, else the CA last used on the website
- emails the account about the new login, if it has an email address

## pkiaas logout

Log out of a PKIaaS server.

```
pkiaas logout [flags]
```

Log out: revoke the token on the server and delete it from this computer.

With `--all`, every CLI login of your account is revoked, on every computer. Use it if a token may have leaked.

This command calls the PKIaaS server.

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--all` | bool | revoke every CLI login of your account, on every computer |
| `--server` | string | the PKIaaS server (default: the last one you logged in to) |

Examples:

```sh
pkiaas logout
pkiaas logout --all
```

With `--json`, the result is an object with these fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `server` | string | the server logged out of |
| `revoked` | integer, optional | with `--all`, how many logins were revoked on the server |
| `removedLocalToken` | boolean | whether a token stored on this computer was deleted |

Side effects:

- revokes the token on the server (with `--all`, every CLI login of the account)
- deletes the stored token
- forgets the active CA for the server

## pkiaas pkcs12

Create PKCS#12 (.pfx/.p12) files on this computer.

```
pkiaas pkcs12 [flags]
```

Commands:

- [`pkiaas pkcs12 create`](reference.md#pkiaas-pkcs12-create)

## pkiaas pkcs12 create

Combine a key and its certificate into a PKCS#12 file.

```
pkiaas pkcs12 create --key FILE --cert FILE --out FILE [flags]
```

Combine a private key, its certificate and the CA chain into a PKCS#12 (.pfx/.p12) file.

`--cert` may hold the whole chain (e.g. a fullchain.pem); the certificate whose public key matches the key is
used, and the others are added as the chain, followed by any in `--chain`.

The file is protected with AES-256-CBC, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 and an HMAC-SHA256 MAC, which Windows 10 1709 and
later, macOS, Java 12 and later, and OpenSSL 1.1.1 and later read. `--legacy` uses 3DES and a SHA-1 MAC for older
systems. `--no-passphrase` writes the key unencrypted, for programs that load PKCS#12 files without a password;
protect such a file like a plain private key.

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--cert` | string | the certificate file (PEM; may include the chain). Required. |
| `--chain` | string | a PEM file with the CA certificates |
| `--force` | bool | replace the file if it exists |
| `-k`, `--key` | string | the private key file. Required. |
| `--key-passphrase-env` | string | read the key passphrase from this environment variable. Not with `--key-passphrase-file`. |
| `--key-passphrase-file` | string | read the key passphrase from this file's first line (- for standard input). Not with `--key-passphrase-env`. |
| `--legacy` | bool | use 3DES and SHA-1 for older Windows, macOS and Java |
| `--no-passphrase` | bool | don't encrypt the file |
| `-o`, `--out` | string | the PKCS#12 file to create. Required. |
| `--passphrase-env` | string | read the PKCS#12 password from this environment variable. Not with `--passphrase-file`. |
| `--passphrase-file` | string | read the PKCS#12 password from this file's first line (- for standard input). Not with `--passphrase-env`. |

Examples:

```sh
pkiaas pkcs12 create --key server.key --cert server.pem --chain ca.pem --out server.pfx
pkiaas pkcs12 create --key server.key --key-passphrase-env KEY_PASSPHRASE --cert server.pem --chain ca.pem --out server.pfx --passphrase-env PFX_PASSPHRASE --json
```

With `--json`, the result is an object with these fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | the PKCS#12 file |
| `format` | string | how the file is protected: aes-256, legacy-3des or unencrypted |
| `subject` | string | the certificate's subject |
| `certificates` | integer | how many certificates the file holds, the certificate and its chain |
| `publicKeySha256` | string | the SHA-256 of the public key (DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo), in hex |

Side effects:

- writes the `--out` file, readable by the owner only

## pkiaas version

Show the CLI's version.

```
pkiaas version [flags]
```

Show the CLI's version, and the Go version and platform it was built for. With `--licenses`, show the
licences of the third-party code in the CLI instead (as text, even with `--json`).

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--licenses` | bool | show the licences of the third-party code in the CLI |

Examples:

```sh
pkiaas version --json
pkiaas version --licenses
```

With `--json`, the result is an object with these fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | string | the CLI's version, e.g. 0.1.0+af1cf3e (semantic version + build) |
| `goVersion` | string | the Go version it was built with |
| `os` | string | the operating system it was built for, e.g. linux |
| `arch` | string | the processor architecture it was built for, e.g. amd64 |

## pkiaas whoami

Show who you are logged in as.

```
pkiaas whoami [flags]
```

Show the server and the account the CLI is logged in to, and where the token comes from. Use it to check
for a login: without one, it fails with exit code 3 and the code not_logged_in or invalid_token.

This command calls the PKIaaS server and needs a login.

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--server` | string | the PKIaaS server (default: the last one you logged in to) |

Examples:

```sh
pkiaas whoami --json
```

With `--json`, the result is an object with these fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `server` | string | the server |
| `email` | string or null | the account's email address |
| `displayName` | string or null | the account's name |
| `provider` | string | the identity provider the account signs in with, e.g. google |
| `tokenSource` | string | where the token came from: environment (`PKIAAS_TOKEN`), keyring or file |
